description_full: Itron, Inc., a technology, solutions, and service company, provides end-to-end solutions that help manage energy, water, and smart city operations worldwide. It operates in four segments: Device Solutions, Networked Solutions, Outcomes, and Resiliency Solution. The Device Solutions segment offers hardware products that are used for measurement, control, or sensing, such as standard gas, electricity, water, and communicating meters, as well as heat and allocation products. The Networked Solutions segment provides communicating devices, such as smart meters, modules, endpoints, and sensors; network infrastructure; network design services; and associated heat-end management and application software for acquiring and transporting application-specific data. This segment also products and software for the implementation, installation, and management of communicating devices and data networks; offers industrial internet of things solutions, including automated meter reading; advanced metering infrastructure for electricity, water, and gas; distributed energy resource management; grid edge devices; distribution automation communications; smart lighting; and smart city sensors and applications. The Outcomes segment provides value-added, enhanced software and services, artificial intelligence, and machine learning, statistical modeling, and other analytics. The Resiliency Solutions segment offers software and services. The company offers implementation, project management, installation, consulting, and post-sale maintenance support services, as well as cloud and software-as-a-service; and extended or customer-specific warranties. It offers its products and services under the Itron brand. The company serves utility and smart city customers, and municipalities through its sales force, distributors, agents, partners, and meter manufacturer representatives. Itron, Inc. was incorporated in 1977 and is headquartered in Liberty Lake, Washington.

financial_summary: Itron, Inc. is a mid-cap technology business with a $4.2B market cap on $2.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +10% over the past three years and +2% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 7% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 31%.

The business throws off $383M in free cash flow — roughly 16 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.35× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.6× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 14× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 2.2% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sect: Its 13% operating margin runs 6pp above the Technology median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.56x).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 533 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 13% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 11% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 42% and a beta of 1.17, it moves roughly with the market.
About $49.7M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 52% in the 2020 crash, 39% in the 2022 bear market and 67% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $92.12 (margin of safety -4%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 19%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $67.38 to $130 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Technology peers: P/E 15.6 vs 27.4, EV/EBITDA 13.3 vs 17.1 and P/FCF 11.0 vs 26.1 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 41% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 9.1% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 6.2% (vs the 8% bar).
The 9 covering analysts target $129 on average, 34% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 7% falls short of the cost of capital of 9.0%, so growth at these returns destroys value; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 5.79).
It runs a 31% gross margin and converts 16% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: a Piotroski score of 7/9 and cash conversion of 1.35x.
ROE of 18% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.2x equity multiplier).
Operating margin is running 9pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
It spends 8.7% of revenue on R&D and 2.6% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.6x net debt to EBITDA ($1.0B of cash against $1.2B of debt), with interest covered 13.9x.
Goodwill makes up 36% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 9.7% over 3 years, 1.7% over 5 years and 2.3% over 10 years, so growth is accelerating.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 43.3% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.06 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 89% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 25%.
Capex runs only 0.5x depreciation (1.0% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 15, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own a modest 1.8%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insiders have only sold over the past year (16 sales, net $1.7M sold).
It returns 2.2% a year to shareholders (2.2% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 0.6% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
Short interest is elevated at 19.4% of the float, 8.2 days to cover.
people: With about 4,987 employees, each generates about $475K of revenue, 1.3x the Technology median.
That works out to $77K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.3M (5x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (1/10, lower is better).
